briefs.source_chain: Microsoft and Meta guide above consensus, therefore Goldman raises 2026 hyperscaler capex to $751B from $671B, therefore the four largest buyers pull 2027 orders forward to lock HBM/CoWoS capacity sold out through 1H27, therefore (because the constraint is supply, not appetite) rising HBM contract prices (+18% into 1Q27) push capex guides higher and the cycle extends rather than peaks, therefore Goldman remains Buy NVDA $250 target, with invalidation being two consecutive months of falling HBM contract prices, and a Fed decision is not expected to matter.
briefs.brief_chain: Microsoft and Meta guide above consensus, therefore Goldman raises 2026 hyperscaler capex to $751B from $671B, therefore the mechanism is supply not appetite as the four largest buyers pull 2027 orders forward to lock sold-out HBM/CoWoS capacity through 1H27, therefore rising HBM contract prices (+18% into 1Q27) push capex guides higher so the cycle extends rather than peaks, therefore Buy NVDA $250 target, with invalidation being two consecutive months of falling HBM contract prices, and a Fed decision is not expected to change the picture.

distortions.what: Brief drops 'remain' from 'We remain Buy on NVDA', rendering it as a flat 'Buy NVDA, $250 target' without signaling this is a reiterated (not new) rating.
distortions.would_the_trade_change: No — direction (long), instrument (NVDA), and target ($250) are all identical; only the new-vs-reiterated framing is lost.
